rounds.name: T-01 walking skeleton
rounds.scope: PR-1 walking skeleton: the common.identity probe and the bundle lifecycle (capture, baseline approve, verify, diff, report). The platform profiles of SPEC-0471 are not implemented, so TF06-AC1 to TF06-AC4 are not claimed.

platforms.toolchain: go1.27.1 darwin/amd64, built and run from the source tree
platforms.notes: The 3 skips are the Windows-only and Linux-only cases, skipped with an explicit reason.

platforms.executed_on: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic, x86_64, unprivileged user
platforms.toolchain: test binaries and skillctl cross-compiled from this commit with go1.27.1 darwin/amd64, CGO_ENABLED=0. The unit-test binaries are self-contained and ran without invoking Go. The acceptance script calls go version once for its own evidence header; that host has go1.26.4 installed and Go therefore fetched the go1.26.6 toolchain named by go.mod into the throwaway HOME, which needed network access.
platforms.notes: Read-only towards the host: every run used a throwaway HOME and wrote only inside a temporary directory. The one exception to offline operation is the go version call described under toolchain.
Nothing was executed on Windows. The first real execution is the windows-latest CI job after the push, on a Windows Server image, not a Windows 11 workstation.

rounds.name: T-03 Linux and Ubuntu bastion
rounds.scope: The nine Linux probes (identity, packages, users, sudo, ssh, systemd, mounts, listeners, firewall, containers), privilege capability resolution, the ubuntu-bastion profile, and the contract gaps (capture --actor, split clock skew, doctor checks). Routes, DNS and executable hashes are NOT implemented, so the profile is not yet complete against SPEC-0471 TF06-R3; that is a separate work package.

platforms.executed_on: two hosts: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS kernel 6.17 (trial class) and Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS kernel 6.8 (bastion class, ngrok and MinIO present)
platforms.toolchain: skillctl cross-compiled from this commit with go1.27.1 darwin/amd64, CGO_ENABLED=0, executed on both hosts

runs.note: firewall, effective sshd state, the sudoers files and the container socket are refused without root, and the bundle names each refusal instead of showing an empty list

runs.privilege: elevated (operator ran it explicitly, the tool never elevates itself)
runs.note: the two unsupported probes are common.git and common.claude, which are not built yet (T-02)

platforms.capability_resolution: 10 privilege capabilities on the bastion class host, each with its sources: sudo rules, group membership, container runtime socket access, authorized keys. On the trial class host additionally three privileged containers.

platforms.note: the Linux probes report unsupported with platform_not_supported here, which is the point of the platform guard; the bundle lifecycle, seal, verify, diff and report are exercised by the 62 step acceptance script
vet clean and the test binaries link; nothing executed. The windows-latest CI job of the pull request is the first execution.

defects_found_by_these_runs: the redaction marker contained a colon and broke colon separated records, which dropped the root account from the bundle
the same break in getent group
a container runtime installed as a snap was reported as not present instead of not found
template units aborted whole systemctl batches, leaving 47 units without runtime state
the redactor hid PasswordAuthentication and the sudo NOPASSWD flag, the very statements the scan exists for
five findings rated critical that were a visibility difference, not drift

gates.note: pre-existing: the same dangling references exist on the base commit 26194006e353, in the drift and agent-bundle code and docs plus one placeholder id in a verbaudit test. This branch adds none. The ids are not repeated here, because naming them in a public-plane file would itself be a new violation.
